title: Introduction to UMG 🧩
description: Discover Unreal Motion Graphics and create your first Widget Blueprint.

slides.title: What is UMG? 🖥️
slides.content:
# Unreal Motion Graphics

UMG is Unreal's system for building **2D user interfaces** that overlay the 3D world.

* **Widgets** – buttons, text, images, progress bars
* **Widget Blueprints** – visual scripting for UI logic
* **Canvas Panel** – layout container where you design

*Analogy:* UMG is like a **HUD designer toolkit** – you drag elements onto a canvas and wire them up like Blueprints.

quizData.question: What does UMG stand for?
quizData.explanation: UMG stands for Unreal Motion Graphics, the engine's UI system.

slides.title: Widget Blueprint 👶
slides.content:
# Your UI Container

A **Widget Blueprint** is a special Blueprint for UI logic. It has:

* **Designer** tab – drag and drop widgets visually.
* **Graph** tab – Blueprint graph for UI behaviour.
* **Palette** – list of available widgets (Button, Text, Image, etc.).

Create one: Content Browser → right‑click → **User Interface → Widget Blueprint**. Name it `WBP_HUD`.

quizData.question: Widget Blueprints use the same Event Graph system as Actor Blueprints.
quizData.explanation: Yes, Widget Blueprints have an Event Graph where you can add events and functions just like in Actor Blueprints.

slides.title: Adding a Widget to the Screen 📺
slides.content:
## Display It!

To show the widget during gameplay:

1. In the **Level Blueprint** or any Actor Blueprint, use the **Create Widget** node.
   - Set the Class to your `WBP_HUD`.
2. Connect to an **Add to Viewport** node.
3. (Optional) Store the returned widget reference in a variable to update it later.

You can also use a **Player Controller** or **Game Mode** to auto‑display the HUD on start.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Use the BeginPlay Event

In your Player Controller, call Create Widget and Add to Viewport on Event BeginPlay. This ensures the UI appears as soon as the game starts.
